prompt_en: Photographic cosmic horror at the limits of human knowledge. The frame records an unknown presence; its discovery defeats ordinary understanding. On a refrigerated marine-biology workbench, a squat quartz observation cell fills the left two thirds of the photograph. Inside it, a wet, pale slate-colored tissue ribbon lies threaded through a square measuring lattice. The near part is thin enough to pin under a small steel clip, with a sharp contact shadow on the grid. Follow that same unbroken surface behind the lattice: it opens into a succession of enormous ribbed folds, each receding farther into a dense black interior, as if the small sample has become a cavern that the chamber cannot contain. The repeated fine pores and a single dark longitudinal vein continue from the clipped foreground edge into those distant vaults, making this visibly one continuous material. The last two grid bars bend away into that depth while the front bars remain straight. Keep the whole quartz cell outer rim in view as a small bounded perimeter resting on the bench. Within that finite rim, the receding tissue keeps its own thin enclosing edge, readable separately from the carrier rim. The small irregular specimen rests on its inner steel lattice support, with a clear strip of empty space between the specimen and the quartz wall. Show that support contact, the separating gap, both enclosing edges and the immense interior together. At frame right, the reference-guided person is working as a researcher, shown from the chest upward in three-quarter profile. Use the supplied portrait only as face-and-hair appearance guidance for the researcher. Her face has a soft oval contour, large dark brown eyes, a small straight nose and natural pink lips; her hair is a chin-length black bob with wispy separated bangs. She wears a plain pale work coat. Her right elbow stays close to her ribs, the gloved right hand holding a withdrawn sampling probe horizontally above its metal cradle. Her head has turned toward the sample and her parted lips and fixed gaze show the pause before she can complete that ordinary movement. A closed notebook under her resting left forearm provides an everyday counterweight to the impossible depth. Photograph this as a physically present laboratory discovery with moist surfaces, scratched steel and faint condensation. The camera is at workbench height on a shallow diagonal, using a natural 50mm perspective; keep the clipped tissue, the receding folds and the person's face legible together. A cold inspection lamp grazes the tissue from the left, while soft overhead fluorescence holds the facial detail. Restrained gray-green color and quiet exposure let the small containment frame and the immense interior carry the dread.

h_f2_material_decisions.rationale: Source review 0 in composition-comparison.md. Missing native primary-human/adult portrait context; this is a nonhuman-led scene. Applying only a readable face would clip it; the face/hair preservation is already independently requested.

No microscopy capture is independently established; the actual 50mm shared cell-and-face view is a different capture mode. Its sample context alone does not grant native authority for microscopy.

Source review 2 in composition-comparison.md. A2-rim-support-gap retains the entire existing-owner relation: the already frozen quartz cell is sample_carrier, receding ribbed folds are interior_structure, and small containment frame is exterior_rim. The depth idea is already in the baseline. Only the added complete rim and separately readable tissue edge are a source contribution; final literal is recorded in source-contribution.json. A2 improves boundary legibility over baseline/A1 without inventing a room doorway or any missing owner. H-F2 native_approval remains false.

Source review 3 in composition-comparison.md. Whole meaning requires small distinct fragments and a coherent water/sediment carrier plus size reference. The baseline has one continuous tissue ribbon, not fragments in water or sediment. No chemical microplastic claim follows from a bright dot; adding the full carrier/fragment system would make a second scientific subject rather than clarify the selected specimen.

Source review 4 in composition-comparison.md. Underwater quadrat capture requires a sampling boundary, scale reference, substrate texture and water-column visibility together. The frozen lab scene establishes no underwater camera view, substrate or water column. Borrowing its word boundary while omitting that whole capture would be a fragment; no such adoption is made.

Source review 5 in composition-comparison.md. Source requires phase_transition context and a driving gradient linking nuclei/interfaces/parent and new phases. Those phases and gradient are absent from the frozen discovery. The quartz cell alone is not phase-transition evidence; adding only a transparent vessel would not realize the source.

Source review 7 in composition-comparison.md.
